1131	the Navigation Paradox paper §c.1 names as the residual failure mode
1132	after large context windows (shipped v0.14.0 as
1133	`archy_high_risk_modules` / `edit_risk`). Detailed roadmap entries in
1134	[`FUTURE.md`](../FUTURE.md). The §c.4 paper below
1135	adds two more, both low-cost and both reusing the existing layer
1136	machinery: convention-based layer inference and a layer-presence
1137	check.
1138	
1139	**c.4. Constraint Decay (May 2026)**
1140	([arxiv:2605.06445][constraint-decay]). The paper asks whether LLM
1141	coding agents can generate backend systems that satisfy *structural*
1142	constraints (architecture, database, ORM) rather than merely passing
1143	functional tests, across 80 greenfield and 20 feature-implementation
1144	tasks built from a shared OpenAPI spec (RealWorld Conduit). The
1145	headline result is **Constraint Decay**: as structural requirements
1146	accumulate from baseline (L0) to fully specified (L3), assertion pass
1147	rates fall ~30 percentage points (the strongest configuration drops
1148	95.6% to 78.6%), and the single most expensive *architectural*
1149	constraint is **Clean Architecture layering at -9.1±1.6 pp** in
1150	isolation (specifying a database engine costs more, -19.3 pp; ORM
1151	adherence is near-zero, -0.6 to -1.5 pp). The failures persist on
1152	feature-implementation tasks against existing codebases, so they are
1153	not an artifact of building from scratch. Crucially, the agents
1154	received static prompts describing the architecture but **no dynamic
1155	course-correction** on violations during generation. The study's
1156	ground-truth oracle is a static verifier checking (1) **layer
1157	presence** (at least 3 of 4 canonical layers - routes, services,
1158	repositories, models - exist as separate directories, with an alias
1159	map so `routes`/`handlers`/`routers`/`views` all count as one layer)
1160	and (2) **dependency direction** (a file in a lower-rank layer
1161	importing from a higher-rank layer is a violation).
1162	
1163	Two implications for archy, both sharper than the earlier citations:
1164	
1165	- The verifier's dependency-direction rule **is** archy's `forbid`-rule
1166	  check (`find_violations` in `src/archy/layers.py`), and the
1167	  transitive version is `archy contracts`. The paper independently
1168	  reinvented archy's core check as its measurement instrument, which
1169	  validates the *category*, not just individual metrics: archy already
1170	  ships the harder version of the thing the study had to build, and
1171	  the quantified -9.1 pp shows that an architectural constraint handed
1172	  to the agent as static prose, with no course-correction, measurably
1173	  degrades output, which is the gap archy's feedback loop is designed
1174	  to close (the paper does not itself test archy or any feedback loop).
1175	- The study's explicit gap, "no dynamic course-correction", is exactly
1176	  archy's MCP loop. But it surfaces two capabilities archy does *not*
1177	  yet have, both motivated directly. **Convention-based layer
1178	  inference**: the verifier's alias map lets it check any repo with
1179	  zero config, whereas archy requires a hand-written `layers:` block,
1180	  so a greenfield repo or an agent on an unfamiliar codebase gets no
1181	  layering feedback at all. **Layer-presence check**: archy gates
1182	  forbidden edges but never asserts that an expected layer *exists*, so
1183	  the degenerate single-file solution the paper says agents produce
1184	  passes archy's layer gate silently. Both become roadmap items in
1185	  `FUTURE.md`. The v0.15.0 lesson (archy.yaml-to-Forbidden auto-
1186	  translation was demoted because it manufactured permanent CI false-
1187	  positives it could not whitelist) constrains the design: inference
1188	  ships as an **advisory, agent-facing report, not a CI gate**, in the
1189	  same diagnostic-not-axis spirit as `archy dsm`.
1190	
1191	The paper's largest failure cluster - data-layer defects (bad query
1192	composition 25.5%, ORM runtime violations 21.2%, auth misconfiguration
1193	22.6%; logic errors are ~71% of all failures) - is semantic, not
1194	structural, and stays out of archy's scope per the anti-goals (no
1195	replacement of linters / type checkers). The structural-leak variant
1196	(forbidding DB/ORM imports above the repository layer) was considered
1197	and rejected as a built-in because it would require maintaining a
1198	framework-specific DB/ORM package allowlist; a user who has defined
1199	layers can already express it as their own `forbid` rule.
1200	
1201	*Reception and caveats* ([HN discussion][constraint-decay-hn]).
1202	Several threads sharpen archy's reading. **Supporting:** the top
1203	architecture comment proposes exactly archy's model - adopt an
1204	ArchUnit-style framework to "spoon feed the LLM what exactly it's
1205	doing wrong," treating architectural rules as *executable constraints
1206	rather than prose guidelines* (archy is that, for Python, over MCP);
1207	a second thread notes agents do markedly better when a *deterministic
1208	feedback loop* like a compiler lets them iterate, which is the
1209	structural analog archy provides for the import graph; a third names
1210	a failure the paper does not measure but archy is well-placed to fix,
1211	**cross-session decay**: "architectural rules an agent wrote down on
1212	Monday don't reach the agent making the next change on Tuesday." A
1213	persisted `.importlinter` / `archy.yaml` plus an always-on MCP server
1214	*is* the durable cross-session architecture memory that prose
1215	CLAUDE.md notes are not. One commenter correctly counters that
1216	Markdown prompts *also* persist across model generations (and survive
1217	dependency/API churn better than code), so durability alone is not the
1218	wedge: the distinction is that prose persists but is never *enforced*,
1219	whereas a config is persisted **and checked deterministically every
1220	session**. Durable-and-enforced is the claim, not durability; and that
1221	is the part independent of model strength. **Tempering:** the single
1222	top comment flags that **frontier models were not fully tested, for
1223	cost reasons**, so the absolute pass-rate numbers are directional, not
1224	definitive; others argue the effect may partly rebrand known
1225	long-context degradation ("context rot") and that some of it erodes as
1226	models improve. Net: treat the -9.1 pp layering penalty as *evidence
1227	the feedback loop has value, not as a fixed constant*, and lean
1228	hardest on the cross-session-persistence argument.
1229	
1230	**A sharper mechanism than the paper states: aspiration vs consequence
1231	constraints.** The thread's most load-bearing observation is that
1232	agents *ignore* aspirational constraints ("be modular", "follow Clean
1233	Architecture") but *obey* brief, precise, preventative rules ("a file
1234	in this layer must not import that one") "because it is brief,
1235	unambiguous, and precise." This is the mechanism behind the paper's
1236	own -9.1 pp layering penalty: Clean Architecture, as handed to the
1237	agent in prose, *is* an aspiration, so it decays; the identical
1238	constraint expressed as a directional `forbid` edge is a consequence,
1239	and consequences get obeyed. The implication sharpens the #122/#135
1240	inference design directly: the inferred layering report must emit
1241	**consequence-shaped negative rules** (resolved `X must not import Y`
1242	pairs), never aspirational prose, or it reproduces the exact failure
1243	the paper measures. It also yields the cleanest one-line statement of
1244	archy's value the docs currently lack: **archy converts architectural
1245	aspirations into checkable consequences.**
1246	
1247	Two further threads converge on *timing* and *division of labor*.
1248	**Calcification** (one commenter, 2B tokens on a C compiler):
1249	architectural patterns self-reinforce once they dominate the context,
1250	so constraints applied up front stick while constraints retrofitted
1251	after the agent has calcified a different pattern do not. This is
1252	independent support for the timing of archy's loop (risk/affected
1253	*before* edits; the pre-edit `archy install --hooks` framing) and
1254	argues for surfacing the dominant existing pattern at task start.
1255	**Single-objective optimization**: a separate commenter frames
1256	constraint decay as the impossibility of optimizing two objectives at
1257	once (functional + non-functional); the design consequence is that
1258	offloading the *structural* objective to an external deterministic
1259	checker frees the agent's budget for the *functional* one, which is
1260	precisely archy's role.
1261	
1262	**Two features these threads motivate, both larger than they first
1263	look** (filed as Deferred epics in [`FUTURE.md`](../FUTURE.md), not Next
1264	items):
1265	
1266	- *Positive exemplar surfacing.* The thread's most-repeated practical
1267	  claim is that showing the agent a good example beats describing the
1268	  rule ("exemplar-based constraints proved phenomenally powerful"; a
1269	  separate report of ~75-80% style-match when the agent could see how
1270	  a pattern was already implemented). archy today is purely negative -
1271	  it ranks violations (`archy check`) and fragile modules
1272	  (`archy_high_risk_modules`); the inverse, ranking the *cleanest*
1273	  existing module as a copy-me template, is the highest-payoff
1274	  technique in the thread and has no roadmap item. It is **not small**,
1275	  and the obvious framing (build a corpus of patterns) is a trap; the
1276	  design question - corpus vs project-relative, and what archy can
1277	  legitimately claim given it only sees the graph - is worked through
1278	  in §14c.5 below.
1279	- *Rule-rot / constraint-staleness detection.* One commenter names a
1280	  failure the paper does not measure: agents obey constraints but
1281	  cannot judge when a constraint itself should *change*, so a stale
1282	  rule gets satisfied by inelegant indirection rather than revised. The
1283	  mirror image of constraint decay is rule rot, and archy can see the
1284	  symptom (a `forbid` rule carrying many `ignore_imports` exceptions,
1285	  or a layer boundary accumulating indirection edges that exist only to
1286	  route around it - the psycopg-through-db-engine shape from the v0.15
1287	  lesson). This is **also large**: distinguishing "the rule is stale"
1288	  from "the code is wrong" is the hard part and needs the same FP-rate
1289	  discipline as the dead-code study (§12) before anything ships.
1290	
1291	### 14c.5. Positive exemplar surfacing: why it is project-relative, not a corpus
1292	
1293	Of the two §14c.4 epics, exemplar surfacing has the larger design
1294	trap, and it is worth resolving on paper before any code. The naive
1295	reading - "ship a curated corpus of good patterns and best practices
1296	the agent can copy" - is wrong for archy on five independent grounds,
1297	and the literature is unusually clear about each.
1298	
1299	**1. The pattern space is combinatorial and the implementations vary
1300	without bound.** Design-pattern-detection research has a standing
1301	result that "patterns are only a guideline ... each pattern can be
1302	implemented in various ways," which is exactly why classical static
1303	detectors "struggle with the complexity and variability of real-world
1304	pattern implementations" and the field has moved to LLM-based
1305	detection ([LLM-Based Design Pattern Detection][dp-llm],

### 14c.6. Code cleanliness and the change-spread non-result (why #260 did not ship a metric)

The SonarSource minimal-pair study ([arxiv:2605.20049][cleanliness],
"Does Code Cleanliness Affect Coding Agents?", Claude Sonnet 4.6 in
Claude Code, Python + Java) is the sharpest agent-footprint evidence to
date, and it prompted a proposed archy feature (#260): a *change-spread
/ grep-targetability guard* that would compute each candidate module's
historical git **co-change degree** as a proxy for agent navigation
cost, and warn on god-object splits to "keep a single grep-targetable
anchor rather than scatter logic across files." An adversarial research
pass (18 sources, 25 claims through 3-vote verification, 2026-07-17)
concluded the metric would be **theater**, and the feature was
downscoped to this note. The reasoning is worth recording because it is
a reusable anti-theater template.

**What the paper actually establishes (the part that survives).** In
aggregate, the *cleaner* variant **shrinks** the agent's footprint:
input tokens -7.1%, output -8.5%, reasoning -11.1%, and file
revisitation **-34%** (the largest effect), concentrated on
**multi-module** tasks. Crucially, **there is no pass-rate effect**
(+0.1 pp; and on Claude Code specifically a separate study found no
significant health-vs-unhealth break-rate difference, 96.19% vs 94.81%,
p=0.439 [ai-friendliness][ai-friendliness]). So cleanliness moves
*cost*, not *capability*. Any archy claim here must be scoped to
footprint, never correctness.

**Why the change-spread metric is theater (four failures).**

1. *The motivating result is a single-task anecdote below the noise
   floor.* The "+8% input tokens from extraction scatter" (the paper's
   Case 2, `genie/cluster-active-job-limit`) is one exemplar of a
   *tension*, not a powered finding. The 13-task cognitive-hotspot track
   where helper-extraction actually happens is **footprint-neutral**
   (+1.8% input tokens, the authors' word is "essentially unchanged"),
   not negative. Per-task input-token deltas span -47% to +44%, and the
   paper itself states a single per-task delta around 10% "may be agent
   noise rather than signal" - input tokens vary **2.5x** on repeated
   runs of the *same* task. Case 2's +8% even runs *counter* to the
   pooled -7% direction, the signature of task-specific noise. Building a
   ranking or annotation on Case 2 is fitting to noise.
2. *Historical git co-change degree is not a validated proxy for agent
   navigation.* The one 2026 study on co-committal
   ([doi:10.3390/software5010011][co-committal], 5 repos, 14k+ commits)
   concludes it indicates evolutionary coupling only "in certain
   scenarios," with usefulness that "depends on project-specific
   development practices" and link strength "strongly influenced by the
   development style ... of contributing developers." A majority of
   co-evolving classes are not structurally linked at all. And **no**
   agent-navigation paper tests co-change against agent file-reads: the
   ones that study navigation (CodeCompass §14c.1; ContextBench
   [arxiv:2602.05892][contextbench]) operationalize **structural
   AST/import** dependencies, which archy already computes. Co-change
   measures human commit habit; the design silently reinterpreted it as
   an agent-navigation cost, unvalidated.
3. *No study supports a tooling intervention that flags change-spread.*
   The evidence is descriptive. With no measured pass-rate effect and a
   token-only, directional, single-config (one model, one harness,
   2026-preprint) result, "keep a grep anchor" is advice dressed as a
   metric. Several 2026 claims that such structural/scaffolding
   interventions add little over the base model (the "bitter lesson")
   verified as *more* supported than their negations.
4. *archy already ships the signal the literature actually
   operationalizes.* The navigation bottleneck the papers name is
   *navigational salience* (§14c.1), and the structural predictor they
   use is AST/import coupling - which is precisely `edit_risk`
   (propagation cost x instability x fan-in, §14c.3) and `archy_impact`.
   A git-co-change "change_spread" field would be a second, weaker,
   redundant proxy for a signal archy surfaces better structurally.

**What this leaves.** `archy_what_to_refactor_next` stays as-is; #260
ships no metric and no ranking change. The one honest, hedged takeaway -
that a *cleaner* structure tends to shrink an agent's navigation
footprint (not its success rate), and that a decomposition is most
footprint-friendly when it stays grep-targetable rather than scattering
logic - is recorded here as a documented caveat, not surfaced as a
quantified tool output. This is the anti-theater line: the paper is real
and useful positioning evidence (cleanliness lowers agent *cost*), but
it does not license a per-module change-spread number, so archy does not
manufacture one. The reusable rule: an external paper motivates a
*claim*; a shippable metric additionally needs a *validated proxy* and a
stake beyond the noise floor, and #260 had neither.

# bench: agent-footprint minimal-pair validation (does an archy-recommended refactor cut agent tokens + revisitation?)

## Summary

Add a new bench harness that empirically tests archy's core claim in the terms the 2026 coding-agent literature now uses: **does applying an archy-recommended refactor reduce a coding agent's token footprint and file-revisitation on a fixed task?**

This is motivated by Trivedi & Schmitt (SonarSource), *"Does Code Cleanliness Affect Coding Agents? A Controlled Minimal-Pair Study"*, arXiv 2605.20049v1 (https://arxiv.org/html/2605.20049v1), discussed on HN (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48798815). All claims below were adversarially fact-checked against the primary source.

## What the paper found (verified quotes)

- **Pass rate is flat**: "the pass rate changes by less than a percentage point between sides (0.913 on cleaner code, 0.921 on messier code = -0.9 pp)." Cleanliness does not change *whether* the task gets done.
- **Footprint shrinks on cleaner code**: "Input tokens fall 7.1% ... Output tokens fall 8.5% ... Reasoning characters ... drop 11.1% ... Conversation messages drop 7.0%."
- **Largest single effect is file revisitation**: "on the cleaner side, the agent returns to files it has already edited 34% less often" (dataset aggregate; ~"a third", not "halved" — the "roughly half" figure is the multi-module track only).
- **Where the effect concentrates**: the multi-module track (tasks spanning >=2 modules) "carries the experiment's strongest footprint contrast ... Most of the dataset-level footprint reduction ... comes from this track."

## Why this is the highest-leverage item for archy

The paper's headline effect concentrates on **cross-module / cross-seam tasks**, driven by **file revisitation** (the agent looping back to files it already touched). That is exactly the layer archy operates at (`coupling`, `dsm`, `cycles`, `impact`).

**Honest framing caveat (do not overstate):** the paper does NOT test module-dependency tooling, and its own manipulated cleanliness lever was SonarQube *line-level* rule violations, with an intra-file god-method-decomposition mechanism. "archy's module layer targets the effect layer" is a reasonable **inference from where the payoff concentrated (cross-module tasks)**, not a paper finding. This experiment is how we'd actually test it instead of asserting it.

A result like "applying archy's top `what_to_refactor_next` recommendation cut agent input tokens by X% and revisitation by Y% on this task, with no test regression" would be a genuinely novel, defensible claim at the exact layer archy owns. Today `bench/*_sweep.py` measures architecture metrics on real repos; **none of it measures agent token footprint** — this is a new bench category.

## Proposed design (minimal-pair, before/after)

Reuse the paper's protocol, but close its #1 acknowledged gap:

1. Pick a repo + a fixed, externally-described task (inputs/outputs only, names no files — per the paper's task rules).
2. **Variant A** = repo as-is. **Variant B** = repo with archy's top `what_to_refactor_next` / coupling recommendation applied as a *behavior-preserving, test-gated* refactor.
3. Run the same agentic task (Claude Code) on both; capture input/output tokens, reasoning chars, conversation messages, distinct files read, and **file revisitations**.
4. **Add the regression gate the paper admits it lacks**: run the repo's full pre-existing test suite on both variants and assert no unrelated regressions. Paper §6: "We do not check whether the agent broke unrelated tests already present in the repository."

## Guardrails learned from validating the paper

- **Behavior-preserving variants, not LLM-synthesized.** The paper built variants with an agent pipeline ("Slopify"/"Vibeclean"); HN's top skeptic (id 48800911) attacks exactly this plus the missing regression control. Our edge: use *real archy-recommended* refactors, test-gated. (Note: the widely-repeated "Opus 4.6 built the variants" claim is an HN commenter's assertion, NOT in the paper — the paper never names the construction model.)
- **Tokens, not dollars.** Paper §6: the token->dollar mapping "is nonlinear" and configuration-dependent. Report footprint, not cost guarantees.
- **One config risk.** Paper ran only Sonnet 4.6 / Claude Code. Note the same limitation on any result we publish.

## References

- Paper: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.20049v1
- Prior art on agent-cost-as-eval-axis (anchor citation): SWE-Effi, arXiv 2509.09853
- HN thread: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48798815
- Slots into `docs/research/RESEARCH_METRICS.md` §14 (AI-agent-specific framing) / §14c and the `bench/` harness.

#259 is genuinely a new bench *category*: unlike the existing `*_sweep.py` metric harnesses, it has to run a real coding agent (Claude Code headless) and parse its transcript for token footprint + file revisitation, gated by the repo's test suite. Two things make the full experiment heavy: it needs API budget, and the paper's own **2.5× per-task token variance** means a single run is worthless (it needs many repetitions per variant, plus a chosen repo/task/refactor).

So there's a real scope fork on this first PR. Let me confirm before building.

I'm building a benchmark harness that runs Claude Code fully headless (non-interactive) on a fixed coding task and needs to measure the agent's "footprint" from the run. Please give me precise, current answers (with exact field names) on these, and flag anything version-dependent:

1. `claude -p "<prompt>" --output-format json`: what exact fields does the final JSON contain? 3. Where does the full session transcript get persisted on disk (the ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<session-id>.jsonl file), and what is the per-line schema? Is that the most reliable source for a complete tool-call + usage record after a headless run?

6. Any flags to make runs more reproducible / reduce variance (temperature, seed, --max-turns), and known caveats about headless runs for benchmarking?

Be concrete about exact CLI flags and JSON keys. If something isn't available, say so plainly so I don't design around a field that doesn't exist.

Based on my inspection of the current Claude Code CLI (v2.1.212) and live headless runs, here are the precise, version-current answers for your benchmark harness:

## 1. `claude -p "<prompt>" --output-format json` — Final JSON Shape

**Exact fields in the result object:**

```json
{
  "type": "result",
  "subtype": "success|error_during_execution|...",
  "is_error": boolean,
  "api_error_status": null|string,
  "duration_ms": number,
  "duration_api_ms": number,
  "ttft_ms": number,
  "ttft_stream_ms": number,
  "time_to_request_ms": number,
  "num_turns": number,
  "result": string,
  "stop_reason": "end_turn|tool_use|...",
  "session_id": string,
  "total_cost_usd": number,
  "usage": {
    "input_tokens": number,
    "cache_creation_input_tokens": number,
    "cache_read_input_tokens": number,
    "output_tokens": number,
    "server_tool_use": {
      "web_search_requests": number,
      "web_fetch_requests": number
    },
    "service_tier": string,
    "cache_creation": {
      "ephemeral_1h_input_tokens": number,
      "ephemeral_5m_input_tokens": number
    },
    "inference_geo": string,
    "iterations": [
      {
        "type": "message",
        "input_tokens": number,
        "output_tokens": number,
        "cache_read_input_tokens": number,
        "cache_creation_input_tokens": number,
        "cache_creation": { ... }
      }
    ],
    "speed": string
  },
  "modelUsage": {
    "<model-identifier>": {
      "inputTokens": number,
      "outputTokens": number,
      "cacheReadInputTokens": number,
      "cacheCreationInputTokens": number,
      "webSearchRequests": number,
      "costUSD": number,
      "contextWindow": number,
      "maxOutputTokens": number
    }
  },
  "permission_denials": [],
  "terminal_reason": "completed|aborted_streaming|...",
  "fast_mode_state": "off|on",
  "uuid": string
}
```

**Key observations:**
- `num_turns`, `total_cost_usd`, `session_id`, and `duration_ms` are all present as you need
- Token fields: `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_creation_input_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens` in both `usage` and per-iteration
- NO reasoning/thinking token count exposed (see #5 below)
- `result` contains the final assistant text response

## 2. `--output-format stream-json` — Per-Message Envelope

Each line is a separate JSON object. Relevant types:

**Assistant message with tool_use:**
```json
{
  "type": "assistant",
  "message": {
    "model": "claude-opus-4-8",
    "id": "msg_...",
    "role": "assistant",
    "content": [
      {
        "type": "tool_use",
        "id": "toolu_...",
        "name": "Read|Write|Edit|Bash|Grep|Glob",
        "input": { /* tool-specific input */ },
        "caller": { "type": "direct" }
      },
      {
        "type": "text",
        "text": "..."
      },
      {
        "type": "thinking",
        "thinking": "",
        "signature": "base64-encoded-encrypted-thinking"
      }
    ],
    "usage": {
      "input_tokens": number,
      "cache_creation_input_tokens": number,
      "cache_read_input_tokens": number,
      "output_tokens": number,
      "service_tier": string,
      "inference_geo": string
    }
  },
  "parent_tool_use_id": null|string,
  "session_id": string,
  "uuid": string,
  "timestamp": ISO8601,
  "request_id": string
}
```

**User message with tool_result:**
```json
{
  "type": "user",
  "message": {
    "role": "user",
    "content": [
      {
        "type": "tool_result",
        "tool_use_id": "toolu_...",
        "content": "stdout/output-text",
        "is_error": boolean
      }
    ]
  },
  "session_id": string,
  "uuid": string,
  "timestamp": ISO8601,
  "tool_use_result": {
    "stdout": string,
    "stderr": string,
    "interrupted": boolean,
    "isImage": boolean,
    "noOutputExpected": boolean
  }
}
```

**Important:** Tool_use blocks appear in `message.content[]` with `type: "tool_use"`. User/tool_result messages do NOT carry usage; usage is only on assistant messages.

For stream-json, you must use `--verbose` (else you get an error).

## 3. Session Transcript Persistence

**Path:** `~/.claude/projects/<project-slug>/<session-id>.jsonl`

Example: `/Users/hosanglee/.claude/projects/-Users-hosanglee-archy/3f0e5416-fe5b-4862-9f7e-d8ccb5f5c8cd.jsonl`

**Schema (per line, JSONL format):** Each line is a JSON object with `type` field. Key types:

| type | content | usage? | tool calls? |
|------|---------|--------|-------------|
| `assistant` | Full message with content blocks | YES | YES (tool_use blocks) |
| `user` | User text or tool_result | NO | (tool_result blocks) |
| `system` | Hooks, metadata, stop reasons | NO | NO |
| `attachment` | File snapshots, context | NO | NO |
| `file-history-snapshot` | File state at message | NO | NO |
| `last-prompt` | User's last prompt | NO | NO |
| `mode`, `permission-mode`, `ai-title` | Session config | NO | NO |

**Reliability:** The JSONL transcript is the most complete source. It includes usage per message AND tool calls. It persists locally immediately after the session ends. For benchmarking, parse it to count:
- Distinct files touched: extract all `"name": "Read|Write|Edit|Grep"` tool_use blocks and the file paths in their `input`
- Revisitations: track which files appear in multiple tool_use blocks across the transcript

# Spec: agent-footprint minimal-pair bench (#259)

Status: design (no harness code yet). This spec fixes the protocol, the
telemetry schema, and the anti-theater guardrails before any code or any
(expensive, nondeterministic) live agent run.

## 1. The claim under test

> Does applying an **archy-recommended, behavior-preserving** refactor to a
> repository measurably reduce a coding agent's **token footprint** and
> **file revisitation** on a fixed task, **with no regression** in the repo's
> pre-existing test suite?

This is the first bench in a new category. Every existing `bench/*_sweep.py`
measures an architecture metric over real repos; **none measures agent
behavior**. This one runs a real coding agent (Claude Code, headless) on
before/after variants and parses its transcript.

The framing is deliberately narrow: **footprint (cost), not correctness.** The
motivating study ([arxiv:2605.20049](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.20049v1),
SonarSource) found cleanliness moves footprint but leaves pass rate flat
(+0.1 pp). archy must not claim a capability effect. See
[`docs/research/RESEARCH_METRICS.md` §14c.6](research/RESEARCH_METRICS.md) for
the anti-theater lineage (this bench is the "how we'd test it instead of
asserting it" answer to the #260 non-result).

## 2. Why archy's layer is the interesting place to test it

The paper's footprint effect concentrates on **multi-module tasks** and is
driven by **file revisitation** (the agent looping back to files it already
touched). That is the layer archy operates at (`coupling`, `dsm`, `cycles`,
`impact`, `what_to_refactor_next`).

**Honest caveat, restated so no result overstates it:** the paper's own
manipulated lever was SonarQube *line-level* rule violations plus intra-file
god-method decomposition; it did **not** test module-dependency tooling.
"archy's module layer targets the effect layer" is an *inference from where the
payoff concentrated*, not a paper finding. This bench exists to test that
inference, not to assume it.

## 3. Protocol (minimal-pair, before/after, paired)

1. Choose a repo with a real, green pre-existing test suite, and a fixed task
   described **only** by external behavior (inputs/outputs), naming **no files**
   (the paper's task rule, so file choice is the agent's, not ours).
2. **Variant A** = repo as-is (`HEAD`).
   **Variant B** = repo with archy's top `what_to_refactor_next` (or `coupling`)
   recommendation applied as a **behavior-preserving, test-gated** refactor
   (see §6). A and B differ only by that refactor.
3. Run the identical task with the identical agent config on both variants,
   **N times each** (§8), from a clean checkout per run.
4. Capture one `FootprintRecord` (§4) per run.
5. Run the repo's **full pre-existing test suite** on the agent's output for
   every run and record pass/fail (§7). This is the gate the paper admits it
   lacks (its §6: "We do not check whether the agent broke unrelated tests").
6. Report paired deltas B-vs-A per metric, as a distribution, with the
   regression outcome (§9).

## 4. Telemetry: the `FootprintRecord`

Captured per run. Sources verified against Claude Code CLI v2.1.x headless
output (`--output-format json` for totals; the persisted session transcript
`~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<session-id>.jsonl` for per-tool-call detail, which
is the most complete record: it carries both `usage` on assistant messages and
every `tool_use` block).

| Field | Type | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `variant` | "A"\|"B" | harness | |
| `run_index` | int | harness | 0..N-1 |
| `input_tokens` | int | `usage.input_tokens` | non-cache input |
| `cache_read_input_tokens` | int | `usage.cache_read_input_tokens` | reported separately, never folded silently into `input_tokens` (cache state varies run to run, §8) |
| `cache_creation_input_tokens` | int | `usage.cache_creation_input_tokens` | |
| `output_tokens` | int | `usage.output_tokens` | |
| `num_turns` | int | `num_turns` | proxy for "conversation messages" |
| `distinct_files_touched` | int | transcript | count of unique file paths across all `Read`/`Edit`/`Write` `tool_use` blocks |
| `file_revisitations` | int | transcript | **primary metric.** Count of `Read`/`Edit` `tool_use` blocks on a path that was already `Edit`/`Write`-touched earlier in the same transcript (definition in §5) |
| `duration_ms` | int | `duration_ms` | secondary; wall-clock is noisy |
| `total_cost_usd` | float | `total_cost_usd` | recorded for reference only, never headlined (§9) |
| `test_regression` | bool | harness | true if the pre-existing suite has a new failure vs the variant's own baseline (§7) |
| `task_completed` | bool | `subtype=="success"` and not `is_error` | the agent finished; NOT a correctness claim |
| `model` | str | run config | pinned model id, recorded on every row |

**Dropped metric (be explicit):** the paper's **"reasoning characters"** cannot
be replicated. Claude Code persists `thinking` blocks with the content
**encrypted** (`signature`), and no reasoning/thinking token or char count is
exposed. We do **not** invent a proxy; the metric is simply absent, and any
comparison to the paper says so.

## 5. Metric definitions (so two implementers agree)

- **`distinct_files_touched`**: the size of the set of resolved file paths
  appearing in any `Read`/`Edit`/`Write` tool input over the run.
- **`file_revisitations`**: iterate tool calls in order; maintain the set
  `edited` of paths seen in a prior `Edit`/`Write`. Increment the counter each
  time a `Read`/`Edit` targets a path already in `edited`. This operationalizes
  the paper's "returns to files it has already edited". `Grep`/`Glob`/`Bash` do
  not count as file touches (no single unambiguous target path).
- **Token footprint headline** = `input_tokens + output_tokens` (cache fields
  reported alongside but excluded from the headline, since cache hit/miss is a
  cross-run artifact, not agent effort).

## 6. Variant B construction rules (the edge over the paper)

- **archy-recommended**: B applies the specific refactor archy's
  `what_to_refactor_next` / `coupling` surfaced, not an arbitrary cleanup.
- **behavior-preserving**: the refactor changes structure, not semantics.
- **test-gated**: the repo's full pre-existing suite must pass on B before B is
  admitted (else B is not behavior-preserving and is rejected).
- **human/tool-authored, NOT LLM-synthesized**: the paper built variants with an
  agent pipeline; its top HN critic attacked exactly that plus the missing
  regression control. Our variants are real refactors gated by tests, recorded

# Spec: agent-footprint minimal-pair bench (#259)

Status: design (no harness code yet). This spec fixes the protocol, the
telemetry schema, and the anti-theater guardrails before any code or any
(expensive, nondeterministic) live agent run.

## 1. The claim under test

> Does applying an **archy-recommended, behavior-preserving** refactor to a
> repository measurably reduce a coding agent's **token footprint** and
> **file revisitation** on a fixed task, **with no regression** in the repo's
> pre-existing test suite?

This is the first bench in a new category. Every existing `bench/*_sweep.py`
measures an architecture metric over real repos; **none measures agent
behavior**. This one runs a real coding agent (Claude Code, headless) on
before/after variants and parses its transcript.

The framing is deliberately narrow: **footprint (cost), not correctness.** The
motivating study ([arxiv:2605.20049](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.20049v1),
SonarSource) found cleanliness moves footprint but leaves pass rate flat
(+0.1 pp). archy must not claim a capability effect. See
[`docs/research/RESEARCH_METRICS.md` §14c.6](research/RESEARCH_METRICS.md) for
the anti-theater lineage (this bench is the "how we'd test it instead of
asserting it" answer to the #260 non-result).

## 2. Why archy's layer is the interesting place to test it

The paper's footprint effect concentrates on **multi-module tasks** and is
driven by **file revisitation** (the agent looping back to files it already
touched). That is the layer archy operates at (`coupling`, `dsm`, `cycles`,
`impact`, `what_to_refactor_next`).

**Honest caveat, restated so no result overstates it:** the paper's own
manipulated lever was SonarQube *line-level* rule violations plus intra-file
god-method decomposition; it did **not** test module-dependency tooling.
"archy's module layer targets the effect layer" is an *inference from where the
payoff concentrated*, not a paper finding. This bench exists to test that
inference, not to assume it.

## 3. Protocol (minimal-pair, before/after, paired)

1. Choose a repo with a real, green pre-existing test suite, and a fixed task
   described **only** by external behavior (inputs/outputs), naming **no files**
   (the paper's task rule, so file choice is the agent's, not ours).
2. **Variant A** = repo as-is (`HEAD`).
   **Variant B** = repo with archy's top `what_to_refactor_next` (or `coupling`)
   recommendation applied as a **behavior-preserving, test-gated** refactor
   (see §6). A and B differ only by that refactor.
3. Run the identical task with the identical agent config on both variants,
   **N times each** (§8), from a clean checkout per run.
4. Capture one `FootprintRecord` (§4) per run.
5. Run the repo's **full pre-existing test suite** on the agent's output for
   every run and record pass/fail (§7). This is the gate the paper admits it
   lacks (its §6: "We do not check whether the agent broke unrelated tests").
6. Report paired deltas B-vs-A per metric, as a distribution, with the
   regression outcome (§9).

## 4. Telemetry: the `FootprintRecord`

Captured per run. Sources verified against Claude Code CLI v2.1.x headless
output (`--output-format json` for totals; the persisted session transcript
`~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<session-id>.jsonl` for per-tool-call detail, which
is the most complete record: it carries both `usage` on assistant messages and
every `tool_use` block).

| Field | Type | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `variant` | "A"\|"B" | harness | |
| `run_index` | int | harness | 0..N-1 |
| `input_tokens` | int | `usage.input_tokens` | non-cache input |
| `cache_read_input_tokens` | int | `usage.cache_read_input_tokens` | reported separately, never folded silently into `input_tokens` (cache state varies run to run, §8) |
| `cache_creation_input_tokens` | int | `usage.cache_creation_input_tokens` | |
| `output_tokens` | int | `usage.output_tokens` | |
| `num_turns` | int | `num_turns` | proxy for "conversation messages" |
| `distinct_files_touched` | int | transcript | count of unique file paths across all `Read`/`Edit`/`Write` `tool_use` blocks |
| `file_revisitations` | int | transcript | **primary metric.** Count of `Read`/`Edit` `tool_use` blocks on a path that was already `Edit`/`Write`-touched earlier in the same transcript (definition in §5) |
| `duration_ms` | int | `duration_ms` | secondary; wall-clock is noisy |
| `total_cost_usd` | float | `total_cost_usd` | recorded for reference only, never headlined (§9) |
| `test_regression` | bool | harness | true if the pre-existing suite has a new failure vs the variant's own baseline (§7) |
| `task_completed` | bool | `subtype=="success"` and not `is_error` | the agent finished; NOT a correctness claim |
| `model` | str | run config | pinned model id, recorded on every row |

**Dropped metric (be explicit):** the paper's **"reasoning characters"** cannot
be replicated. Claude Code persists `thinking` blocks with the content
**encrypted** (`signature`), and no reasoning/thinking token or char count is
exposed. We do **not** invent a proxy; the metric is simply absent, and any
comparison to the paper says so.

- **`distinct_files_touched`**: the size of the set of resolved file paths
  appearing in any `Read`/`Edit`/`Write` tool input over the run.
- **`file_revisitations`**: iterate tool calls in order; maintain the set
  `edited` of paths seen in a prior `Edit`/`Write`. Increment the counter each
  time a `Read`/`Edit` targets a path already in `edited`. This operationalizes
  the paper's "returns to files it has already edited". `Grep`/`Glob`/`Bash` do
  not count as file touches (no single unambiguous target path).
- **Token footprint headline** = `input_tokens + output_tokens` (cache fields
  reported alongside but excluded from the headline, since cache hit/miss is a
  cross-run artifact, not agent effort).

  `what_to_refactor_next` / `coupling` surfaced, not an arbitrary cleanup.
- **behavior-preserving**: the refactor changes structure, not semantics.
- **test-gated**: the repo's full pre-existing suite must pass on B before B is
  admitted (else B is not behavior-preserving and is rejected).

  agent pipeline; its top HN critic attacked exactly that plus the missing
  regression control. Our variants are real refactors gated by tests, recorded

  result on one model/harness is not a general law. A second model is a
  follow-up, not a blocker.
- **Publish the null.** If applying archy's recommendation does not move
  footprint outside the noise band, that is the result and it ships as such
  (the #260 discipline: we do not manufacture a win).

```

  --model <pinned-model-id> \

Design-first spec for the flagship #259 bench, before any (expensive, nondeterministic) harness code or live agent run. Part of #259.

- Docs-only. No harness code yet; `bench/agent_footprint.py` (parse_transcript / run_variant / run_pair) and the first live pair are the follow-up. The deterministic transcript parser is the unit-test boundary (testable against a fixture, no live agent).

content.text:
**PR #280** is up ([link](https://github.com/hslee16/Archy/pull/280)) — the #259 design spec, DeepWork-reviewed clean.

## What the spec locks down

**`docs/SPEC_AGENT_FOOTPRINT_BENCH.md`** fixes the protocol before any expensive/nondeterministic code:

- **Claim under test:** does an archy-recommended, behavior-preserving, *test-gated* refactor cut a coding agent's token footprint + file revisitation on a fixed task, with no test regression?
- **`FootprintRecord` schema** mapped to *verified* Claude Code headless fields (I had the claude-code-guide agent confirm the exact JSON keys + transcript format against CLI v2.1.x).
- **The regression gate the paper lacks** (full pre-existing suite on both variants).

Two facts from that verification directly shaped the design and kept it honest:
1. **"Reasoning characters" is dropped, not faked** — Claude Code encrypts thinking blocks, so that paper metric isn't reproducible. The spec says so instead of inventing a proxy.
2. **No seed/temperature/max-turns exist** + the paper's **2.5× per-task variance** → the spec mandates **N≥10 interleaved runs with a paired distribution**; a single pair is explicitly not a result.

=== bench/_common.py ===
"""Shared helpers for the bench sweep scripts.

Extracted so `hotspots_sweep.py` and `duplicates_sweep.py` (and any future
sweep) share one manifest loader and one clone/checkout routine instead of
copy-pasting them. Sweep scripts are run as `python bench/<name>.py`, so
`bench/` is on `sys.path[0]` and this module imports as `from _common import ...`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

import yaml  # type: ignore[import-untyped]

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
MANIFEST = REPO_ROOT / "bench" / "projects.yaml"
WORKDIR = Path("/tmp/archy_bench")


def load_manifest() -> list[dict]:
    return yaml.safe_load(MANIFEST.read_text())["projects"]


def clone_or_update(proj: dict) -> Path | None:
    """Clone/checkout a project at its pinned SHA; never raises -- on any failure
    return None so the caller can skip the project and keep the sweep going. The
    archy self-entry uses REPO_ROOT directly (its pin may name a tag that does
    not exist yet during a release PR)."""
    name = proj["name"]
    sha = proj["sha"]
    if name == "archy":
        return REPO_ROOT
    target = WORKDIR / name
    if not target.exists():
        WORKDIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        res = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "clone", "--quiet", f"https://github.com/{proj['repo']}.git", str(target)],
        )
        if res.returncode != 0:
            return None
    has_sha = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "-C", str(target), "cat-file", "-e", sha],
        capture_output=True,
    )
    if has_sha.returncode != 0:
        subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(target), "fetch", "--quiet", "origin"], check=False)
    if (
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "-C", str(target), "checkout", "--quiet", sha],
        ).returncode
        != 0
    ):
        return None
    subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(target), "reset", "--hard", "--quiet", sha], check=False)
    subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(target), "clean", "-fdx", "--quiet"], check=False)
    return target

Good question, and I should correct my imprecise phrasing: **CI does not need an API key.** CI runs only the deterministic `parse_transcript` unit test against a recorded fixture — no agent is invoked. """Agent-footprint minimal-pair bench (#259).

Runs a coding agent (Claude Code, headless) on before/after variants of a repo
and measures its token footprint and file revisitation on a fixed task. See
`docs/SPEC_AGENT_FOOTPRINT_BENCH.md` for the full protocol, metric definitions,
and the anti-theater guardrails this harness must honor.

Two layers, deliberately split:

* `parse_transcript` is the **deterministic core**: a persisted Claude Code
  session `.jsonl` transcript -> a `ParsedTranscript` of token sums and
  file-touch metrics. It invokes no agent and is unit-tested in
  `tests/test_agent_footprint.py` against a synthetic fixture.
* `run_variant` / `run_pair` are the **live runner**: they invoke `claude -p`
  headless, copy the persisted transcript, and run the repo's test suite as the
  regression gate the paper lacks. They need `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and real agent
  time, so they run only when this file is executed directly, never in CI.

Sweep scripts are run as `python bench/agent_footprint.py`, so `bench/` is on
`sys.path[0]`; keep imports self-contained.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import shutil
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import NamedTuple

# Tool names that name a single target file (their `file_path` input is the
# touched path). Grep/Glob/Bash are excluded: they have no single unambiguous
# target, so they do not count as a file touch (spec section 5).
_READ_TOOLS = frozenset({"Read"})
_WRITE_TOOLS = frozenset({"Edit", "Write", "MultiEdit", "NotebookEdit"})
_FILE_TOOLS = _READ_TOOLS | _WRITE_TOOLS

# Default tool surface handed to the agent; pinned so the two variants see an
# identical, reproducible tool set (spec section 10).
DEFAULT_ALLOWED_TOOLS = ("Read", "Write", "Edit", "Bash", "Grep", "Glob")


class ParsedTranscript(NamedTuple):
    """Everything derivable from a session transcript alone (no run config).

    Token fields are summed across every assistant message: each assistant
    message carries the usage for *its own* generation, so the sum is the total
    the run consumed. `cache_read_input_tokens` is reported separately and never
    folded into the footprint headline, because cache hit/miss is a cross-run
    artifact, not agent effort (spec section 4).
    """

    input_tokens: int
    cache_read_input_tokens: int
    cache_creation_input_tokens: int
    output_tokens: int
    assistant_messages: int
    distinct_files_touched: int
    file_revisitations: int

    @property
    def footprint_tokens(self) -> int:
        """Headline token footprint: non-cache input + output (spec section 5)."""
        return self.input_tokens + self.output_tokens


class FootprintRecord(NamedTuple):
    """One agent run's full footprint row: parsed transcript + run context."""

    variant: str
    run_index: int
    model: str
    input_tokens: int
    cache_read_input_tokens: int
    cache_creation_input_tokens: int
    output_tokens: int
    num_turns: int
    distinct_files_touched: int
    file_revisitations: int
    duration_ms: int
    total_cost_usd: float
    task_completed: bool
    test_regression: bool

    @property
    def footprint_tokens(self) -> int:
        return self.input_tokens + self.output_tokens


def _iter_tool_uses(message: dict):
    """Yield (tool_name, file_path|None) for each tool_use block, in order."""
    for block in message.get("content", []):
        if not isinstance(block, dict) or block.get("type") != "tool_use":
            continue
        name = block.get("name", "")
        file_path = None
        if name in _FILE_TOOLS:
            raw = (block.get("input") or {}).get("file_path")
            if raw:
                # Normalize so "a/../a/x.py" and "a/x.py" are one file; the agent
                # is usually consistent within a run, but normpath makes the
                # distinct/revisit counts robust to trivial path variation.
                file_path = os.path.normpath(str(raw))
        yield name, file_path


def parse_transcript(path: str | Path) -> ParsedTranscript:
    """Parse a persisted Claude Code session `.jsonl` into footprint metrics.

    Deterministic and agent-free: this is the unit-test boundary. Token sums
    come from the `usage` on assistant messages; file metrics come from their
    `tool_use` blocks, walked in transcript order so revisitation is causal.

    Revisitation (the paper's "returns to files it has already edited", spec
    section 5): maintain the set of paths already written (`Edit`/`Write`);
    every subsequent `Read`/`Edit` of a path already in that set is one
    revisitation. The first write of a file is not a revisit; a read *before*
    any write is not a revisit.
    """
    path = Path(path)
    in_toks = cache_read = cache_create = out_toks = 0
    assistant_messages = 0
    touched: set[str] = set()
    written: set[str] = set()
    revisitations = 0

    with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for line in fh:
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            try:
                entry = json.loads(line)
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                continue
            if entry.get("type") != "assistant":
                continue
            message = entry.get("message", {})
            assistant_messages += 1

            usage = message.get("usage") or {}
            in_toks += int(usage.get("input_tokens", 0) or 0)
            cache_read += int(usage.get("cache_read_input_tokens", 0) or 0)
            cache_create += int(usage.get("cache_creation_input_tokens", 0) or 0)
            out_toks += int(usage.get("output_tokens", 0) or 0)

            for name, file_path in _iter_tool_uses(message):
                if file_path is None:
                    continue
                touched.add(file_path)
                if name in _READ_TOOLS or name in _WRITE_TOOLS:
                    if file_path in written:
                        revisitations += 1
                if name in _WRITE_TOOLS:
                    written.add(file_path)

    return ParsedTranscript(
        input_tokens=in_toks,
        cache_read_input_tokens=cache_read,
        cache_creation_input_tokens=cache_create,
        output_tokens=out_toks,
        assistant_messages=assistant_messages,
        distinct_files_touched=len(touched),
        file_revisitations=revisitations,
    )


# --- live runner (needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; never invoked in CI) --------------


def _project_slug(repo_dir: Path) -> str:
    """Claude Code's on-disk project dir name: the abs path with '/' -> '-'."""
    return str(repo_dir.resolve()).replace("/", "-")


def _locate_transcript(repo_dir: Path, session_id: str) -> Path:
    """Path to the persisted session transcript for a headless run."""
    return Path.home() / ".claude" / "projects" / _project_slug(repo_dir) / f"{session_id}.jsonl"


def _run_claude(repo_dir: Path, task_prompt: str, *, model: str, allowed_tools) -> dict:
    """Invoke `claude -p` headless in `repo_dir`; return the parsed JSON result.

    `--bare` isolates hooks / CLAUDE.md / MCP so the repo under test, not the
    local environment, is the variable. Requires `claude` on PATH and
    ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the environment.
    """
    cmd = [
        "claude",
        "-p",
        task_prompt,
        "--output-format",
        "json",
        "--model",
        model,
        "--dangerously-skip-permissions",
        "--bare",
        "--allowedTools",
        ",".join(allowed_tools),
        "--setting-sources",
        "local",
    ]
    proc = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=repo_dir, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"claude exited {proc.returncode}: {proc.stderr[:500]}")
    return json.loads(proc.stdout)


def _run_test_gate(repo_dir: Path, test_cmd: list[str], baseline_failed: bool) -> bool:
    """Return True if the agent's output regressed the pre-existing suite.

    `baseline_failed` is whether the pristine variant's own suite was already
    red; a regression is a suite that passed at baseline but fails after the
    agent's edits. A variant whose baseline is already red cannot be used to
    detect regressions, so it returns False (and the caller should flag it).
    """
    if baseline_failed:
        return False
    passed = subprocess.run(test_cmd, cwd=repo_dir, capture_output=True).returncode == 0
    return not passed


def run_variant(
    repo_dir: Path,
    task_prompt: str,
    *,
    variant: str,
    run_index: int,
    model: str,
    artifact_dir: Path,
    test_cmd: list[str] | None = None,
    baseline_failed: bool = False,
    allowed_tools=DEFAULT_ALLOWED_TOOLS,
) -> FootprintRecord:
    """Run one agent task on one variant and return its footprint row."""
    result = _run_claude(repo_dir, task_prompt, model=model, allowed_tools=allowed_tools)
    session_id = result["session_id"]

    transcript = _locate_transcript(repo_dir, session_id)
    artifact_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    saved = artifact_dir / f"{variant}_{run_index}_{session_id}.jsonl"
    shutil.copy(transcript, saved)
    parsed = parse_transcript(saved)

    regression = (
        _run_test_gate(repo_dir, test_cmd, baseline_failed) if test_cmd is not None else False
    )

    return FootprintRecord(
        variant=variant,
        run_index=run_index,
        model=model,
        input_tokens=parsed.input_tokens,
        cache_read_input_tokens=parsed.cache_read_input_tokens,
        cache_creation_input_tokens=parsed.cache_creation_input_tokens,
        output_tokens=parsed.output_tokens,
        num_turns=int(result.get("num_turns", parsed.assistant_messages)),
        distinct_files_touched=parsed.distinct_files_touched,
        file_revisitations=parsed.file_revisitations,
        duration_ms=int(result.get("duration_ms", 0)),
        total_cost_usd=float(result.get("total_cost_usd", 0.0)),
        task_completed=(result.get("subtype") == "success" and not result.get("is_error")),
        test_regression=regression,
    )


def run_pair(
    variant_a_dir: Path,
    variant_b_dir: Path,
    task_prompt: str,
    *,
    n: int,
    model: str,
    artifact_dir: Path,
    test_cmd: list[str] | None = None,
) -> list[FootprintRecord]:
    """Run the task n times on each variant, interleaved (A, B, A, B, ...).

    Interleaving averages out any slow drift in the service across the run
    (spec section 8). A single pair is not a result; n >= 10 is the floor.
    """
    records: list[FootprintRecord] = []
    for i in range(n):
        for variant, repo_dir in (("A", variant_a_dir), ("B", variant_b_dir)):
            records.append(
                run_variant(
                    repo_dir,
                    task_prompt,
                    variant=variant,
                    run_index=i,
                    model=model,
                    artifact_dir=artifact_dir,
                    test_cmd=test_cmd,
                )
            )
    return records


def _paired_deltas(records: list[FootprintRecord], metric: str) -> list[float]:
    """Per-run B-minus-A deltas for one metric, matched on run_index."""
    by_run: dict[int, dict[str, FootprintRecord]] = {}
    for r in records:
        by_run.setdefault(r.run_index, {})[r.variant] = r
    deltas = []
    for pair in by_run.values():
        if "A" in pair and "B" in pair:
            deltas.append(float(getattr(pair["B"], metric)) - float(getattr(pair["A"], metric)))
    return deltas


def summarize(records: list[FootprintRecord]) -> dict:
    """Median paired delta + sign count per footprint metric (spec section 9)."""
    metrics = [
        "footprint_tokens",
        "input_tokens",
        "output_tokens",
        "num_turns",
        "distinct_files_touched",
        "file_revisitations",
    ]
    out: dict = {"n_pairs": 0, "metrics": {}, "regressions": 0}
    # footprint_tokens is a property, not a field; expose it via a shim.
    getters = dict.fromkeys(metrics)
    for m in metrics:
        deltas = (
            [
                r_b - r_a
                for r_a, r_b in _paired_footprint(records)
            ]
            if m == "footprint_tokens"
            else _paired_deltas(records, m)
        )
        if not deltas:
            continue
        out["n_pairs"] = len(deltas)
        out["metrics"][m] = {
            "median_delta": statistics.median(deltas),
            "b_lower_count": sum(1 for d in deltas if d < 0),
            "b_higher_count": sum(1 for d in deltas if d > 0),
            "tie_count": sum(1 for d in deltas if d == 0),
        }
    out["regressions"] = sum(1 for r in records if r.test_regression)
    return out


def _paired_footprint(records: list[FootprintRecord]) -> list[tuple[float, float]]:
    by_run: dict[int, dict[str, FootprintRecord]] = {}
    for r in records:
        by_run.setdefault(r.run_index, {})[r.variant] = r
    pairs = []
    for pair in by_run.values():
        if "A" in pair and "B" in pair:
            pairs.append((float(pair["A"].footprint_tokens), float(pair["B"].footprint_tokens)))
    return pairs


def _main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Agent-footprint minimal-pair bench (#259)")
    ap.add_argument("--repo-a", required=True, type=Path, help="variant A checkout (as-is)")
    ap.add_argument("--repo-b", required=True, type=Path, help="variant B checkout (refactored)")
    ap.add_argument("--task-file", required=True, type=Path, help="file with the task prompt")
    ap.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=10, help="runs per variant (>= 10; spec section 8)")
    ap.add_argument("--model", required=True, help="pinned model id, recorded on every row")
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=Path("/tmp/archy_footprint"))
    ap.add_argument("--test-cmd", default=None, help="test command for the regression gate")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    if not os.environ.get("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"):
        print("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is required for live runs.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    if args.n < 10:
        print(f"warning: n={args.n} < 10; a single pair is not a result (spec section 8).")

    task_prompt = args.task_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    test_cmd = args.test_cmd.split() if args.test_cmd else None
    records = run_pair(
        args.repo_a,
        args.repo_b,
        task_prompt,
        n=args.n,
        model=args.model,
        artifact_dir=args.out,
        test_cmd=test_cmd,
    )
    summary = summarize(records)
    (args.out / "records.json").write_text(json.dumps([r._asdict() for r in records], indent=2))
    (args.out / "summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))
    print(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(_main(sys.argv[1:]))

    regression = (
        _run_test_gate(repo_dir, test_cmd, baseline_failed) if test_cmd is not None else False
    )

    return FootprintRecord(
        variant=variant,
        run_index=run_index,
        model=model,
        input_tokens=parsed.input_tokens,
        cache_read_input_tokens=parsed.cache_read_input_tokens,
        cache_creation_input_tokens=parsed.cache_creation_input_tokens,
        output_tokens=parsed.output_tokens,

        file_revisitations=parsed.file_revisitations,
        duration_ms=int(result.get("duration_ms", 0)),

        task_completed=(result.get("subtype") == "success" and not result.get("is_error")),

def run_pair(
    variant_a_dir: Path,
    variant_b_dir: Path,
    task_prompt: str,
    *,
    n: int,
    model: str,
    artifact_dir: Path,
    test_cmd: list[str] | None = None,
) -> list[FootprintRecord]:
    """Run the task n times on each variant, interleaved (A, B, A, B, ...).

    Interleaving averages out any slow drift in the service across the run
    (spec section 8). A single pair is not a result; n >= 10 is the floor.
    """
    records: list[FootprintRecord] = []
    for i in range(n):
        for variant, repo_dir in (("A", variant_a_dir), ("B", variant_b_dir)):
            records.append(
                run_variant(
                    repo_dir,
                    task_prompt,
                    variant=variant,
                    run_index=i,
                    model=model,
                    artifact_dir=artifact_dir,
                    test_cmd=test_cmd,
                )
            )
    return records


def _paired_deltas(records: list[FootprintRecord], metric: str) -> list[float]:
    """Per-run B-minus-A deltas for one metric, matched on run_index."""
    by_run: dict[int, dict[str, FootprintRecord]] = {}
    for r in records:
        by_run.setdefault(r.run_index, {})[r.variant] = r
    deltas = []
    for pair in by_run.values():
        if "A" in pair and "B" in pair:
            deltas.append(float(getattr(pair["B"], metric)) - float(getattr(pair["A"], metric)))
    return deltas


def summarize(records: list[FootprintRecord]) -> dict:
    """Median paired delta + sign count per footprint metric (spec section 9)."""
    metrics = [
        "footprint_tokens",
        "input_tokens",
        "output_tokens",
        "num_turns",
        "distinct_files_touched",
        "file_revisitations",
    ]
    out: dict = {"n_pairs": 0, "metrics": {}, "regressions": 0}
    # footprint_tokens is a property, not a field; expose it via a shim.
    getters = dict.fromkeys(metrics)
    for m in metrics:
        deltas = (
            [
                r_b - r_a
                for r_a, r_b in _paired_footprint(records)
            ]
            if m == "footprint_tokens"
            else _paired_deltas(records, m)
        )
        if not deltas:
            continue
        out["n_pairs"] = len(deltas)
        out["metrics"][m] = {
            "median_delta": statistics.median(deltas),
            "b_lower_count": sum(1 for d in deltas if d < 0),
            "b_higher_count": sum(1 for d in deltas if d > 0),
            "tie_count": sum(1 for d in deltas if d == 0),
        }
    out["regressions"] = sum(1 for r in records if r.test_regression)
    return out


def _paired_footprint(records: list[FootprintRecord]) -> list[tuple[float, float]]:
    by_run: dict[int, dict[str, FootprintRecord]] = {}
    for r in records:
        by_run.setdefault(r.run_index, {})[r.variant] = r
    pairs = []
    for pair in by_run.values():
        if "A" in pair and "B" in pair:
            pairs.append((float(pair["A"].footprint_tokens), float(pair["B"].footprint_tokens)))
    return pairs


def _main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Agent-footprint minimal-pair bench (#259)")
    ap.add_argument("--repo-a", required=True, type=Path, help="variant A checkout (as-is)")
    ap.add_argument("--repo-b", required=True, type=Path, help="variant B checkout (refactored)")
    ap.add_argument("--task-file", required=True, type=Path, help="file with the task prompt")
    ap.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=10, help="runs per variant (>= 10; spec section 8)")
    ap.add_argument("--model", required=True, help="pinned model id, recorded on every row")
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=Path("/tmp/archy_footprint"))
    ap.add_argument("--test-cmd", default=None, help="test command for the regression gate")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    if not os.environ.get("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"):
        print("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is required for live runs.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    if args.n < 10:
        print(f"warning: n={args.n} < 10; a single pair is not a result (spec section 8).")

    task_prompt = args.task_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    test_cmd = args.test_cmd.split() if args.test_cmd else None
    records = run_pair(
        args.repo_a,
        args.repo_b,
        task_prompt,
        n=args.n,
        model=args.model,
        artifact_dir=args.out,
        test_cmd=test_cmd,
    )
    summary = summarize(records)
    (args.out / "records.json").write_text(json.dumps([r._asdict() for r in records], indent=2))
    (args.out / "summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))
    print(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))
    return 0

    raise SystemExit(_main(sys.argv[1:]))

import sys
from pathlib import Path

def _assistant(usage: dict, tool_uses: list[tuple[str, str | None]]) -> dict:
    """A synthetic Claude Code transcript `assistant` line."""
    content: list[dict] = []
    for name, file_path in tool_uses:
        block: dict = {"type": "tool_use", "id": f"toolu_{name}", "name": name, "input": {}}
        if file_path is not None:
            block["input"]["file_path"] = file_path
        content.append(block)
    return {"type": "assistant", "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": content, "usage": usage}}

    # User/tool_result lines carry no usage and no tool_use; the parser must skip
    # them for token sums so they cannot inflate the footprint.
    return {"type": "user", "message": {"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "content": text}]}}

    path.write_text("\n".join(json.dumps(entry) for entry in lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

    """A 4-turn run with a known-by-hand set of expected metrics.

    Sequence of file touches:

      m2 Edit a.py     (a not yet written -> no revisit; a now written)
      m3 Read a.py     (a written -> REVISIT #1) + Write b.py (new -> no revisit; b written)
      m4 Edit b.py     (b written -> REVISIT #2)
    Plus a Grep and a Bash that must NOT count as file touches, and a
    user/system line that must NOT contribute tokens.
    """
    _write_transcript(
        path,
        [
            {"type": "system", "subtype": "init"},
            _assistant(
                {"input_tokens": 100, "output_tokens": 50, "cache_read_input_tokens": 1000, "cache_creation_input_tokens": 200},

                [("Read", "a.py"), ("Write", "b.py"), ("Bash", None)],

    base.update(over)
    return af.FootprintRecord(**base)

# Agent-footprint bench: results

Protocol and metric definitions: [`docs/SPEC_AGENT_FOOTPRINT_BENCH.md`](../docs/SPEC_AGENT_FOOTPRINT_BENCH.md).
Harness: [`bench/agent_footprint.py`](agent_footprint.py). Parser unit tests:
`tests/test_agent_footprint.py`.

## Status

**Harness landed; no live numbers yet.** The deterministic core
(`parse_transcript`, `summarize`) is implemented and CI-tested against a
synthetic transcript fixture. The live runner (`run_variant` / `run_pair`)
invokes `claude` headless and needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` plus real agent time,
so it is run out of band, not in CI. The first live minimal-pair (below) is the
next step; this file will carry its numbers when it runs.

## First live-pair target (chosen, not yet run)

Selected by running archy on the candidate, so variant B applies a *real*
archy recommendation rather than an arbitrary cleanup.

- **Repo:** `pallets/flask` @ `36e4a82` (already pinned in `bench/projects.yaml`;
  ~5.5k commits of history, so churn and co-change signals are populated).
- **Test gate:** flask's own suite, `pytest -q` (the regression gate of spec
  section 7; a variant is only admitted if the pristine suite is green).
- **Variant B refactor (archy's #1 `what_to_refactor_next`, fused lens):**
  decompose **`flask.sansio.app`** (`src/flask/sansio/app.py`, the `App` base
  class). archy ranks it first by a wide margin:

  ```
  1. flask.sansio.app  [hotspot+edit_risk]  priority=1.837
     complexity x churn hotspot (cc_sum=87, churn=508) AND high edit-risk
     (risk=0.40: central and fragile)
  2. flask.cli          priority=1.295
  3. flask.helpers      priority=1.025
  ```

  It is a genuine god-object (the central Flask application base class), and its
  co-change partner `flask.globals` shows up as the top hidden-coupling pair
  (`conf=0.68`, 15 co-commits), so edits here already ripple. The variant-B diff
  keeps `App`'s public behavior identical (the full suite must stay green) while
  splitting the class so a typical edit lands in one grep-targetable place
  instead of scattering across the god-class.

- **Task (externally described, names no files, per the paper's task rule):** a
  Flask feature/bug task whose natural implementation touches the
  application-configuration / blueprint-registration surface that lives in
  `App` (so it spans `sansio.app` + `blueprints` + `ctx`), phrased purely by
  input/output behavior. Exact wording is fixed at run time and recorded
  verbatim with the results.

- **Runs:** `n >= 10` per variant, interleaved; report the paired B-minus-A
  distribution (median delta + sign counts), never a single pair.

Why flask: a dominant, unambiguous archy recommendation on a real god-object; a
fast, green, well-known test suite for the gate; and an app-centric task that
spans modules, which is where the paper's footprint effect concentrates.

## Reading these numbers (when they exist)

- **Footprint, not correctness.** No pass-rate claim; cleanliness moved
  footprint but not pass rate in the motivating study (§14c.6 of
  `RESEARCH_METRICS.md`). `task_completed` means the agent finished, not that it
  was correct.
- **Tokens, not dollars** in any headline; `total_cost_usd` stays in the raw
  table only.
- **One-config caveat:** every result names the exact model and CLI flags; one
  model/harness is not a general law.
- **Publish the null.** If applying archy's recommendation does not move
  footprint outside the noise band (the paper saw ~2.5x per-task variance, hence
  `n >= 10`), that is the result and it ships as such.

_No results table yet; this section fills in when the first pair runs._

content.text:
**PR #281** is up ([link](https://github.com/hslee16/Archy/pull/281)) — the #259 harness, DeepWork-reviewed.

## What shipped

| Piece | What it does |
|-------|-------------|
| `bench/agent_footprint.py` | `parse_transcript` (deterministic core: token sums + file/revisitation metrics from a session `.jsonl`), `run_variant`/`run_pair` (live headless runner + test-regression gate, never in CI), `summarize` (paired B−A deltas) |
| `tests/test_agent_footprint.py` | 6 CI-gated unit tests for the parser against a synthetic transcript — token sums, distinct files, the revisitation-ordering rule, path normalization, malformed-line skipping, paired summary |
| `bench/agent_footprint_results.md` | Status + the first live-pair target, grounded by running archy: flask `sansio.app` (its dominant #1 recommendation) |

**Verification:** 856 passed / 2 skipped, ruff + ty clean. Review found 3 items on the parser — I fixed two (wrapped `os.path.normpath` in a justified helper; extracted the duplicated `footprint_tokens`) and dismissed one (NamedTuple vs pydantic) with the `CoChangeData` precedent, which the reviewer accepted on re-review.

## Where #259 stands

The **harness + first-target selection are done**; what remains is the **live experiment** — author the behavior-preserving `flask.sansio.app` decomposition (variant B, gated green by flask's suite), then run N≥10 interleaved pairs and write the numbers into `agent_footprint_results.md`. That's a budgeted, nondeterministic step (needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and real agent time), so it's a natural stopping point on the code side.

Want me to merge #281? After that, the live run is the next move whenever you're ready to spend the agent time — or we can pick up another backlog thread.

Deterministic and agent-free: this is the unit-test boundary. Token sums
    come from the `usage` on assistant messages; file metrics come from their
    `tool_use` blocks, walked in transcript order so revisitation is causal.

    Revisitation (the paper's "returns to files it has already edited", spec
    section 5): maintain the set of paths already written (`Edit`/`Write`);
    every subsequent `Read`/`Edit` of a path already in that set is one
    revisitation. The first write of a file is not a revisit; a read *before*
    any write is not a revisit.
    """
    path = Path(path)
    in_toks = cache_read = cache_create = out_toks = 0
    assistant_messages = 0
    touched: set[str] = set()
    written: set[str] = set()
    revisitations = 0

    with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for line in fh:
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            try:
                entry = json.loads(line)
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                continue
            if entry.get("type") != "assistant":
                continue
            message = entry.get("message", {})
            assistant_messages += 1

            usage = message.get("usage") or {}
            in_toks += int(usage.get("input_tokens", 0) or 0)
            cache_read += int(usage.get("cache_read_input_tokens", 0) or 0)
            cache_create += int(usage.get("cache_creation_input_tokens", 0) or 0)
            out_toks += int(usage.get("output_tokens", 0) or 0)

            for name, file_path in _iter_tool_uses(message):
                # file_path is non-None only for a file tool (Read/Edit/Write),
                # so any such touch of an already-written path is a revisit.
                if file_path is None:
                    continue
                touched.add(file_path)
                if file_path in written:
                    revisitations += 1
                if name in _WRITE_TOOLS:
                    written.add(file_path)

    return ParsedTranscript(
        input_tokens=in_toks,
        cache_read_input_tokens=cache_read,
        cache_creation_input_tokens=cache_create,
        output_tokens=out_toks,
        assistant_messages=assistant_messages,

def _main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Agent-footprint minimal-pair bench (#259)")
    ap.add_argument("--repo-a", required=True, type=Path, help="variant A checkout (as-is)")
    ap.add_argument("--repo-b", required=True, type=Path, help="variant B checkout (refactored)")
    ap.add_argument("--task-file", required=True, type=Path, help="file with the task prompt")
    ap.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=10, help="runs per variant (>= 10; spec section 8)")
    ap.add_argument("--model", required=True, help="pinned model id, recorded on every row")
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=Path("/tmp/archy_footprint"))
    ap.add_argument("--test-cmd", default=None, help="test command for the regression gate")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    if not os.environ.get("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"):
        print("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is required for live runs.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    if args.n < 10:
        print(f"warning: n={args.n} < 10; a single pair is not a result (spec section 8).")

    task_prompt = args.task_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    test_cmd = args.test_cmd.split() if args.test_cmd else None
    records = run_pair(
        args.repo_a,
        args.repo_b,
        task_prompt,
        n=args.n,
        model=args.model,
        artifact_dir=args.out,
        test_cmd=test_cmd,
    )
    summary = summarize(records)
    (args.out / "records.json").write_text(json.dumps([r._asdict() for r in records], indent=2))

# Agent-footprint bench: results

Protocol and metric definitions: [`docs/SPEC_AGENT_FOOTPRINT_BENCH.md`](../docs/SPEC_AGENT_FOOTPRINT_BENCH.md).
Harness: [`bench/agent_footprint.py`](agent_footprint.py). Parser unit tests:
`tests/test_agent_footprint.py`.

## Status

**Harness landed; no live numbers yet.** The deterministic core
(`parse_transcript`, `summarize`) is implemented and CI-tested against a
synthetic transcript fixture. The live runner (`run_variant` / `run_pair`)
invokes `claude` headless and needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` plus real agent time,
so it is run out of band, not in CI. The first live minimal-pair (below) is the
next step; this file will carry its numbers when it runs.

## First live-pair target (chosen, not yet run)

Selected by running archy on the candidate, so variant B applies a *real*
archy recommendation rather than an arbitrary cleanup.

- **Repo:** `pallets/flask` @ `36e4a82` (already pinned in `bench/projects.yaml`;
  ~5.5k commits of history, so churn and co-change signals are populated).
- **Test gate:** flask's own suite, `pytest -q` (the regression gate of spec
  section 7; a variant is only admitted if the pristine suite is green).
- **Variant B refactor (archy's #1 `what_to_refactor_next`, fused lens):**
  decompose **`flask.sansio.app`** (`src/flask/sansio/app.py`, the `App` base
  class). archy ranks it first by a wide margin:

  ```
  1. flask.sansio.app  [hotspot+edit_risk]  priority=1.837
     complexity x churn hotspot (cc_sum=87, churn=508) AND high edit-risk
     (risk=0.40: central and fragile)
  2. flask.cli          priority=1.295
  3. flask.helpers      priority=1.025
  ```

  It is a genuine god-object (the central Flask application base class), and its
  co-change partner `flask.globals` shows up as the top hidden-coupling pair
  (`conf=0.68`, 15 co-commits), so edits here already ripple. The variant-B diff
  keeps `App`'s public behavior identical (the full suite must stay green) while
  splitting the class so a typical edit lands in one grep-targetable place
  instead of scattering across the god-class.

- **Task (externally described, names no files, per the paper's task rule):** a
  Flask feature/bug task whose natural implementation touches the
  application-configuration / blueprint-registration surface that lives in
  `App` (so it spans `sansio.app` + `blueprints` + `ctx`), phrased purely by
  input/output behavior. Exact wording is fixed at run time and recorded
  verbatim with the results.

- **Runs:** `n >= 10` per variant, interleaved; report the paired B-minus-A
  distribution (median delta + sign counts), never a single pair.

Why flask: a dominant, unambiguous archy recommendation on a real god-object; a
fast, green, well-known test suite for the gate; and an app-centric task that
spans modules, which is where the paper's footprint effect concentrates.

## Reading these numbers (when they exist)

- **Footprint, not correctness.** No pass-rate claim; cleanliness moved
  footprint but not pass rate in the motivating study (§14c.6 of
  `RESEARCH_METRICS.md`). `task_completed` means the agent finished, not that it
  was correct.
- **Tokens, not dollars** in any headline; `total_cost_usd` stays in the raw
  table only.
- **One-config caveat:** every result names the exact model and CLI flags; one
  model/harness is not a general law.
- **Publish the null.** If applying archy's recommendation does not move
  footprint outside the noise band (the paper saw ~2.5x per-task variance, hence
  `n >= 10`), that is the result and it ships as such.

Two findings:

**1. Line 208 — Comment accuracy ("Comments explain WHY... Keep comments accurate. When code changes, update or remove comments that no longer match.")**

```python
# --- live runner (needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; never invoked in CI) --------------
```

This section-header comment says the live runner "needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY," but this directly contradicts the more detailed, more recently-written documentation in the same file: the module docstring ("any auth: an API key or a subscription login, so a logged-in Claude Code session runs them with no key"), the `_run_claude` docstring (lines 233-235, "`claude` authenticates however it is configured: an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or a subscription login, so no key is required inside a logged-in session"), and the `_main` comment (lines 402-406, same point). The line 208 comment is stale/inaccurate relative to the rest of the file's own explanation.

Suggested fix: drop the parenthetical or correct it, e.g. `# --- live runner (needs a working `claude` CLI; never invoked in CI) ---`.

**2. Line 66 (`_normalize_touch_path`) — "pathlib.Path over os.path"**

```python
return os.path.normpath(raw)
```

The convention doc states "Use `pathlib.Path`, not `os.path`" with no stated exception for this case. The function has a well-written WHY comment justifying the choice (pure lexical normalization, no filesystem touch, `Path.resolve()` would be wrong since the repo may not be checked out locally), which is a reasonable engineering rationale — but the author's exception note in this review only pre-approves the `NamedTuple` deviation, not an `os.path` deviation. Since findings exist, I did not call `mark_review_as_passed`. If the parent/author explicitly dismisses these two (e.g., extends the same "justified exception" treatment to the `os.path` case and fixes/accepts the stale comment), the review can be re-run or marked passed accordingly.

Yes — **confirmed working, no API key needed.** Nested `claude -p` inherits this session's subscription login, so the harness runs entirely in-session.

I proved it by running a full `run_variant` here (edit task, 41→42), and it did more than answer the question — it caught three real bugs the synthetic fixture never could:

| Bug | Fix |
|-----|-----|
| `_project_slug` only replaced `/`, so it missed the transcript for any path with `_` | Claude Code sanitizes **every** non-alphanumeric char to `-` |
| `parse_transcript` **triple-counted tokens** — the transcript stores streaming partials of each message (same `message.id`) | Dedupe by message id; totals now match the CLI's own `usage` **exactly** (input 26 / output 456) |
| `--bare` **breaks** `-p` headless in this nested context | Dropped it; use `--setting-sources local` for isolation + `stdin=/dev/null` to avoid a hang |

Plus relaxed `_main` to require only the `claude` CLI (not `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`), and synced the spec §10 + results doc.

**All committed and pushed to PR #281** (new commit `89cd81e`), full suite green (857 passed), DeepWork review clean.

### What this unlocks

We *can* now run the real experiment in-session without a key. But note the honest constraints before spending the agent time:
- **Variant B doesn't exist yet** — someone has to author the behavior-preserving `flask.sansio.app` decomposition (test-gated green) first.
- The paper's **2.5× variance** means N≥10 interleaved runs per variant, and flask's suite runs on each — that's real wall-clock and usage, just billed to the subscription instead of a key.

So the plumbing is ready and validated; the live comparative run is a matter of authoring variant B and letting N≥10 pairs churn.

Want me to **merge #281** first? Then the natural next step is authoring the flask variant-B refactor so we can actually run the pair.
